comments.author: @EnjoyuChinatravel
comments.text: Xinjiang is the one part of China where the sheer scale still catches people off guard — 1.6 million km² means Urumqi down to Kashgar is roughly London to Rome. If you ever make the trip in person: base in Urumqi for Tianchi and the Tianshan foothills, fly down to Kashgar for the old town and the livestock market, and keep Turpan as a separate stop for the grape valleys and those ancient karez irrigation channels. Timing matters more here than anywhere else in China — late April to early June and September to mid-October are the two windows where the desert isn't punishing and the mountain passes are actually open. Doing it overland as one long loop is the mistake most people make; the internal flights are cheap and save you entire days. I put together China itineraries for Enjoyu China Travel (private, customisable tours), so if a Xinjiang route without 12-hour driving days would help with your planning, I'm glad to share one.
